outcome: Birth position dictated by hospital staff
cohort: The study included 7805 mothers from the Cohort'18 Hungarian Birth Cohort Study who gave birth in 2018-2019.
finding: Roma women in Hungary experience significant disadvantages in maternity care, with their ethnic background and socio-economic/regional factors negatively impacting the quality of care they receive, including differences in birth interventions and autonomy.
mod_finding: Roma mothers had a lower rate of caesarean section due to fewer planned interventions, and for vaginal births, they were significantly more likely to have their birth position dictated by hospital staff.
